reply:
`async` functions run on the main thread. They're syntactic sugar for promises—they don't spawn threads or move work anywhere. CPU-heavy code wrapped in `async` still blocks the UI.

To move CPU work off the main thread and stop blocking UI, you need a Web Worker. Post the heavy computation to the worker, let it run there, and message back the result when done.

grade.note: Reply agrees async runs on main thread and correctly recommends Web Workers for CPU-bound work.
